name: AI & Agent Tooling
definition: Software for BUILDING or RUNNING LLM-powered agents: agentic coding agents/CLIs, standalone agent platforms, LLM app frameworks/SDKs, agent workflow builders, and coding-agent skill/config/MCP packs. The repo's reason to exist is orchestrating an LLM to take actions or wiring up agentic apps. POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact is a harness, framework, CLI, plugin pack, or platform whose core job is making an LLM act as an autonomous/assisted agent (calls tools, runs loops, plans, edits code) or helping developers build such agents. NEGATIVE: a model, model weights, a raw inference server, or a training/serving runtime does NOT belong here even though it is 'AI' — send those to ai-ml-runtime. A general application that merely embeds AI features (chatbot UI, image generator app) but isn't an agent framework/platform goes to ai-ml-runtime (generative-ai-app) or self-hosted-app instead.

name: AI Models & Inference Runtimes
definition: Executable ML/AI substrate: deep-learning/ML training frameworks, released model weights + reference implementations, ML/CV inference libraries, LLM inference runtimes/servers, and end-user generative-AI applications (the model or the runtime that runs it IS the product). POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact trains, serves, ships, or directly applies a model — a framework you build models with, downloadable weights, an inference engine/server, a CV library, or a consumer-facing app whose value is generating content from a model. NEGATIVE: a framework/CLI/platform whose job is orchestrating an LLM into an autonomous agent does NOT belong here — send those to ai-agent-tooling. A client SDK that just calls a hosted model API (no model, no inference) goes to dev-tools (client-library-sdk).

name: Frontend & UI Frameworks
definition: Client-side web/UI building blocks: web UI frameworks/libraries, component kits, data-visualization libraries, graphics/3D libraries, animation engines, and frontend app scaffolders. The artifact renders or composes browser/web UI. POSITIVE: belongs here if the repo is a library/framework/kit a developer imports to build web/browser UI, visuals, charts, 3D, or animation. NEGATIVE: a framework that produces NATIVE desktop/mobile binaries goes to cross-platform-app. A finished web application (not a reusable UI library) goes to self-hosted-app. A general dev tool, bundler, or build tool goes to dev-tools (web-build-bundler).

name: Cross-Platform App Frameworks
definition: Frameworks for building NATIVE desktop/mobile/game apps from a single codebase — web-tech-to-native shells, native app frameworks, desktop app shells, and game/app engines. The artifact is the framework others use to ship cross-platform binaries. POSITIVE: belongs here if the repo is a framework/engine/shell whose job is producing native desktop, mobile, or game applications across platforms from one codebase. NEGATIVE: a client-side WEB UI framework or component library (renders in a browser, not native binaries) goes to frontend-ui. A finished cross-platform APP (not the framework) goes to self-hosted-app or dev-tools. A language runtime goes to language-runtime.

name: Languages, Runtimes & Kernels
definition: The foundations you build ON: programming languages + compilers, language execution runtimes/VMs, hardware/platform emulators, and OS kernels. POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact IS a language, compiler, interpreter/VM, emulator, or kernel — the layer beneath applications. NEGATIVE: a server-side web framework or backend platform built IN a language goes to backend-infra. A package/version manager for a language goes to cli-utility. An ML training/inference runtime goes to ai-ml-runtime. A developer SDK/library goes to dev-tools.

name: Backend & Infra Platforms
definition: Server-side platforms and infrastructure developers self-host and run as the backbone of a system: backend/data platforms, infra/container orchestration, database engines/data stores, blockchain nodes, server-side web frameworks, ELT/data-integration, workflow-automation engines, and full-stack app starters/boilerplate. POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact is the running backend, datastore, orchestration layer, or server framework that other apps are built on or deployed onto. NEGATIVE: a complete end-user application you deploy for its own functionality (the app IS the point, not a platform to build on) goes to self-hosted-app. A language execution runtime or compiler goes to language-runtime. An agent platform goes to ai-agent-tooling.

name: Developer Tools & Editors
definition: Runnable developer-facing tools and toolchains: client libraries/SDKs, code editors/IDEs, terminals/consoles, debuggers/language tooling, web build tools/bundlers, security/RE tools, file-format converters, mock-API servers, browser/test automation frameworks, fonts, hardware/firmware projects, and shell/desktop productivity suites. POSITIVE: belongs here if developers run/use the artifact while building software and it is a broad tool, SDK, or toolchain rather than one narrow CLI. NEGATIVE: a narrow single-purpose CLI (downloader, scraper, patch script) goes to cli-utility. An agent/LLM tooling framework goes to ai-agent-tooling. A frontend UI framework/component kit goes to frontend-ui. A self-hosted end-user app goes to self-hosted-app.

name: Self-Hosted & Creative Apps
definition: Complete end-user applications you deploy and run for their own functionality, including desktop GUI apps, creative/visual tools (drawing, diffusion node editors), consumer mobile apps, and monitoring/observability platforms. The app IS the product the user interacts with. POSITIVE: belongs here if the repo is a finished, deployable application whose value is being used directly by an end user, not a framework/library/platform to build other software on. NEGATIVE: a backend/data/infra PLATFORM other apps build on goes to backend-infra. A reusable UI library or component kit goes to frontend-ui. A narrow CLI utility goes to cli-utility. A generative-AI app whose core value is running a model goes to ai-ml-runtime (generative-ai-app).

name: Networking, Remote & Media
definition: Tools that move traffic, sessions, or media streams: proxy GUI clients, reverse proxies/tunnels, remote-desktop control, device control/mirroring, secure file transfer, and media-stream aggregators. POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact's core job is routing/proxying network traffic, establishing remote sessions, mirroring/controlling devices, transferring files, or aggregating media streams. NEGATIVE: a general backend/infra platform or server framework goes to backend-infra. A media DOWNLOADER CLI (grabs a file, not a live stream/session) goes to cli-utility (media-downloader). A self-hosted media app (e.g. a streaming server you deploy as an app) goes to self-hosted-app.

name: CLI Utilities
definition: Focused single-purpose command-line / terminal tools and small API utilities: media downloaders, web-scraping/crawl APIs, package/version managers, system patch/activation scripts, and TUI apps. The whole repo is one sharp CLI capability. POSITIVE: belongs here if the primary interface and value is a narrow command-line utility or scriptable API doing one job well. NEGATIVE: a broad developer tool, IDE, terminal emulator, debugger, or productivity SUITE goes to dev-tools (cli-utility is for narrow single-purpose tools, dev-tools for richer toolchains/editors). A networking/proxy/tunnel CLI goes to networking-media. A general client SDK/library goes to dev-tools (client-library-sdk).

name: Curated Knowledge & Indexes
definition: Non-executable curation and reference data: awesome-lists/ecosystem indexes, OSS discovery feeds, config/template boilerplate, code style/best-practice guides, prompt & tool-internals datasets, security wordlists, protocol/standard specs, and non-software knowledge collections. The repo's value is the curated CONTENT, not runnable code. POSITIVE: belongs here if the artifact is a list, index, dataset, spec, template collection, or reference document meant to be read/referenced rather than executed. NEGATIVE: teaching content with a learning arc (course, tutorial, roadmap, book, build-it project, algorithm-impl collection) goes to learning-resource, not here. A runnable boilerplate that is a working full-stack starter goes to backend-infra (fullstack-app-starter); only static config/template snippets belong here.

name: Learning & Educational Resources
definition: Repos whose artifact is TEACHING content with a learning arc: career roadmaps/study guides, programming courses/tutorials, books/cheatsheet collections, algorithm/reference-impl collections, project-based/build-it tutorials, and interactive curricula/coding schools. POSITIVE: belongs here if the repo exists to teach a human a skill or concept — structured lessons, guided builds, study material, or annotated reference implementations meant for learning. NEGATIVE: a static awesome-list/index, spec, or dataset with no learning arc goes to curated-knowledge. A working tool/library/app that happens to have good docs is NOT a learning resource — file it by what it does. A code style guide goes to curated-knowledge (code-style-guide).

name: Social / Manifesto
definition: Repos whose value is social, political, or manifesto signaling rather than software — labor-rights and social-movement repos, open letters, and advocacy content. POSITIVE: belongs here if the repo exists to express, organize, or signal a social/political/labor stance and contains little to no functional software. NEGATIVE: a curated list or knowledge collection on a social topic that is primarily a reference index goes to curated-knowledge. Any repo with a real runnable artifact should be filed by what the software DOES, not by its cause.

name: Agentic Coding Agent / CLI
definition: The host coding agent itself: a terminal/CLI (or IDE) agent you run that reads and edits a real codebase and executes dev tasks — the thing extensions plug INTO, distinct from a general agent-platform or autonomous-agent-tool. e.g. an open-source terminal coding agent (Claude-Code/Aider/Gemini-CLI-style), an autonomous code-fixing CLI, an IDE agent that drives a repo.

name: Standalone Agent Platform
definition: A self-hostable, runnable AI-agent SYSTEM with its own lifecycle, server/CLI/TUI, and config — a complete product, not a coding-specific CLI (agentic-coding-agent), an imported SDK (llm-app-framework), or a single-loop tool (autonomous-agent-tool). e.g. a multi-agent orchestration server/platform, a self-hosted assistant/chatbot app, an agent runtime with its own UI and persistence.

name: Coding-Agent Skill / Config Pack
definition: Skills, configs, rules, prompts, or MCP/tool packs that plug INTO an existing coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf) and are NOT runnable on their own — pick over agentic-coding-agent (the host) or agent-ecosystem-artifact (tooling that runs around a host). e.g. a Claude Code skills/commands collection, a Cursor rules/.mdc pack, an MCP-server bundle that extends an agent.

name: Coding-Tool Ecosystem Artifact
definition: Tooling that runs AROUND coding agents rather than being one or plugging in as a skill — managers, switchers, datasets, and harnesses (vs agent-extension-pack which loads inside a host). e.g. a provider/model switcher or proxy for coding agents, a GUI/manager for running multiple agents, a dataset of leaked agent system-prompts or an experimental eval harness.

name: LLM App Framework / SDK
definition: Code-level libraries/SDKs you IMPORT to build LLM apps, chains, and agents inside your own program — a dependency, not a standalone app or visual builder (vs llm-app-framework's sibling agent-platform which runs by itself). e.g. an agent/chain orchestration library (LangChain/LlamaIndex-style), a structured-output or RAG SDK, a provider-abstraction client library.

name: Agent Workflow Builder
definition: A low/no-code platform to VISUALLY design, wire, and deploy agentic LLM workflows via a drag-and-drop canvas — the defining trait is the visual builder UI, unlike a code-imported llm-app-framework or a runnable agent-platform. e.g. a node-graph flow builder (Langflow/Flowise-style), a Dify-style LLM-app studio, a visual agent-pipeline designer.

name: Autonomous Agent Tool
definition: A single runnable, goal-driven AI agent that directly performs one kind of task via an autonomous loop — narrower than a full agent-platform and not a coding-repo agent (agentic-coding-agent). e.g. a browser-automation/web agent, an autonomous task/research loop (AutoGPT-style), a single-purpose computer-use agent.

name: ML / Deep-Learning Framework
definition: A low-level toolkit for BUILDING and training neural networks — tensors, autograd, layers, optimizers, GPU kernels — that ships no specific trained model. Route here for the engine you train models WITH, not a model itself. e.g. tensor/autograd frameworks (pytorch, jax), training/distributed libraries, high-level model-building APIs (keras).

name: Model Weights / Reference Impl
definition: A specific released model published as weights plus reference/paper code you LOAD to reproduce or fine-tune, where the repo's identity is that one named model or model family (not a reusable runtime or a general framework). e.g. a single LLM/diffusion release with its reference impl, an architecture's official paper code, a model-card weights repo.

name: LLM Inference Runtime / Server
definition: A general-purpose engine/server that LOADS arbitrary LLM weights and serves inference — model loading, quantization, batching, an OpenAI-style API — without bundling any one specific model or a chat UI. e.g. local LLM serving runtimes (llama.cpp, vllm, ollama), quantization/inference backends, model-agnostic inference servers.

name: ML Model / Inference Capability
definition: A trained model packaged WITH ready-to-run inference code as a drop-in capability you call (input→output), oriented around the task it performs rather than a named weight release or a UI app. e.g. speech-to-text engines (whisper), OCR/detection/embedding pipelines, a vision or audio model exposed as an importable API.

name: Generative-AI Application
definition: An end-user product (UI, chat, or workflow app) that consumes generative AI to produce content for a human, not a library or serving engine — route here if the headline artifact is the user-facing app. e.g. image-generation web UIs (stable-diffusion-webui), local chat/desktop assistants, AI writing/agent apps.

name: Web UI Framework / Library
definition: The core declarative rendering runtime that turns state into DOM, or the meta-framework built on one (routing/SSR) — the engine apps are built ON, not a set of pre-styled widgets. e.g. UI runtimes (React, Vue, Svelte, Solid), meta-frameworks (Next.js, Nuxt, Remix), reactivity/signal libraries.

name: UI Component Kit
definition: Pre-built, styled, accessible UI controls (buttons, dialogs, tables) or CSS frameworks you drop into an app — NOT the rendering runtime itself. e.g. component libraries (shadcn-ui, MUI, Radix), CSS/utility frameworks (Bootstrap, Tailwind), design-system kits.

name: Data Visualization Library
definition: Library for turning datasets into charts/plots/graphs — bound to data and producing analytical visuals, NOT general scene rendering or animation. e.g. charting libs (Chart.js, ECharts, Recharts), data-binding viz toolkits (D3, Vega), graph/network plotters.

name: Graphics / 3D Library
definition: Low-level GPU/canvas rendering and 3D/WebGL engines that draw geometry, meshes, shaders, and scenes — graphics primitives, NOT data charts or DOM UI. e.g. 3D/WebGL engines (Three.js, Babylon.js), WebGPU/canvas renderers, game/graphics engines.

name: Frontend App Scaffolder
definition: A CLI/generator that bootstraps a new frontend project skeleton (config, folders, deps) so you can start coding — a setup tool, NOT a runtime or component library shipped in the app. e.g. project starters (create-react-app, create-vite, create-next-app), framework scaffolders/generators.

name: Native App Framework
definition: A framework whose code compiles/renders to native mobile or desktop UI from a single shared codebase (the framework owns the widget/render layer, not a web view). e.g. Flutter, React Native, .NET MAUI / Kotlin Multiplatform UI toolkits.

name: Desktop App Shell
definition: A shell that wraps an existing web app (HTML/JS) into a distributable native desktop binary, providing the OS window + system bridge rather than its own UI toolkit. e.g. Electron, Tauri, Wails / Neutralino desktop wrappers.

name: Programming Language / Compiler
definition: The source tree of a programming language itself — its compiler, typechecker, parser, or full toolchain — that defines and translates a language. e.g. a language compiler/frontend (Go, Rust), a typechecker/transpiler (TypeScript), a new language project. NOT the VM that runs it (language-runtime) or the OS it targets (os-kernel).

name: Language Runtime
definition: The execution engine, virtual machine, or interpreter that *runs* programs in an already-defined language — the runtime, not the language source. e.g. a JS/TS runtime (Node, Deno, Bun), a language VM/interpreter (CPython, V8, a WASM runtime). NOT the compiler/language itself (programming-language) or a hardware emulator (platform-emulator).

name: Operating System Kernel
definition: The source tree of a low-level operating-system kernel — the core that manages processes, memory, drivers, and hardware directly. e.g. a monolithic/microkernel source (Linux, a hobby OS kernel), a unikernel or RTOS kernel. NOT a userspace runtime (language-runtime) or a hardware emulator (platform-emulator).

name: Backend & Data Platform
definition: An all-in-one server-side platform that bundles a database, auth, and APIs into a single self-hostable Backend-as-a-Service the developer builds an app on top of (not a bare DB engine, not just an HTTP framework). e.g. Firebase/Supabase-style BaaS, Parse/Appwrite-style backend servers, Convex-style reactive app backends.

name: Infra / Orchestration Platform
definition: A platform that schedules, deploys, and manages compute/workloads across machines — the layer that runs and operates services rather than storing app data or serving HTTP. e.g. container orchestrators (Kubernetes/Nomad), service meshes & PaaS control planes, schedulers/cluster managers.

name: Workflow Automation Platform
definition: A self-hostable platform for visually building and running automation flows that connect apps via triggers/actions — the product is the workflow/automation engine, not data-pipeline syncing or generic orchestration. e.g. n8n/Node-RED-style automation, Zapier-like integration builders, low-code workflow engines.

name: Code Editor / IDE
definition: A full code editor, IDE, or editor distribution where developers write and edit source code, including major editor plugins/distros. e.g. a desktop IDE, a Vim/Neovim or VS Code configuration distribution, a browser-based code editor component.

name: Terminal / Console
definition: A terminal emulator, console UI, or shell prompt/multiplexer — the interactive command-line surface itself, not the productivity apps layered on top. e.g. a GPU terminal emulator, a shell prompt/theme engine, a tmux-style multiplexer or terminal-rendering library.

name: File / Format Conversion Tool
definition: A standalone utility whose core job is converting files between formats or encodings. e.g. a document/image format converter, a Markdown-to-PDF/HTML tool, a data-serialization (CSV/JSON/YAML) transcoder.

name: Shell / Desktop Productivity Suite
definition: A broad multi-feature productivity launcher, dotfiles framework, or desktop/shell augmentation suite that bundles many workflow tools rather than doing one thing. e.g. an app launcher/spotlight clone, a dotfiles + window-management suite, an all-in-one shell-config framework like a prezto/oh-my-zsh-style bundle.

name: Self-Hosted Application
definition: A complete, deployable web/server application that the user self-hosts to run a full multi-user service (the catch-all for self-hosted apps that are NOT primarily a desktop GUI binary, a creative/visual canvas, a phone app, or a monitoring stack). e.g. self-hosted photo library (immich), notes/wiki/PKM server, file-sync or media server.

name: Creative / Visual Tool App
definition: A visual/creative-output tool whose core surface is an interactive canvas, editor, or generative pipeline for producing images, diagrams, or media (route here over desktop-gui-app when the point IS making visual artifacts). e.g. drawing/diagram canvas (excalidraw), generative-image node editor (ComfyUI), animation or design tool.

name: Proxy GUI Client
definition: A desktop GUI application that lets a user configure and switch proxy rules to route their own outbound traffic through proxy/VPN protocol engines. Routes the user; never exposes an inbound service (that is reverse-proxy-tunnel). e.g. Clash/Shadowsocks/V2Ray rule-engine front-ends (clash-verge, v2rayN), system-wide proxy switchers, proxy subscription managers.

name: Reverse Proxy / Tunnel
definition: A server/daemon that exposes a service running behind NAT or a firewall to the public internet by tunneling inbound connections through a relay. Inbound exposure of a service, not outbound routing of a user (that is proxy-client). e.g. ngrok-style tunnels, fast reverse proxies (frp), Cloudflare/localhost tunneling daemons.

name: Remote Desktop / Control
definition: Software to remotely view and control the full graphical desktop of another general-purpose computer over the network. A whole PC/desktop session, not a single attached hardware device (that is device-mirroring). e.g. VNC/RDP-style remote desktop tools, peer-to-peer remote support clients (rustdesk), screen-sharing control servers.

name: Device Control / Mirroring
definition: Mirrors the screen of and/or controls a connected hardware device (phone, tablet, embedded board) from a host machine, typically over USB/ADB or a device link. A single attached device, not a full remote computer desktop (that is remote-desktop-control). e.g. Android screen mirroring/control (scrcpy), phone-on-PC display tools, USB device control bridges.

name: Media Stream Aggregator
definition: Collects, curates, or aggregates network media streams (live TV/IPTV/radio playlists) into a unified source for playback. Aggregates content streams, not interactive control of a machine. e.g. IPTV M3U playlist aggregators, live-channel scrapers, stream proxy/EPG collectors.

name: Media Downloader CLI
definition: A command-line tool whose primary job is fetching/extracting audio or video media from web sources and saving it locally. e.g. video/audio rippers (yt-dlp, youtube-dl), playlist/stream downloaders, site-specific media grabbers. NOT a general web data scraper that returns structured text/JSON, and NOT a package downloader.

name: Web Scraping / Crawl API
definition: A service or API that crawls websites and extracts structured/clean web data (text, markdown, JSON) for programmatic or LLM/agent consumption. e.g. crawl-to-markdown APIs (firecrawl), structured extraction scrapers, headless-browser crawl services. NOT a media file downloader, and NOT an interactive terminal app.

name: System Activation / Patch Tool
definition: A script or toolkit that activates, licenses, cracks, or patches already-installed proprietary OS/office software. e.g. OS/office activation scripts (Microsoft-Activation-Scripts), license-bypass patchers, runtime binary patch tools. NOT a package/version manager that installs legitimate dependencies.

name: Awesome List / Ecosystem Index
definition: A static, hand-curated link index that catalogs the libraries/tools/services/resources within one domain — the value is the list itself, not running code. e.g. awesome-* lists, public-apis directories, 'awesome-go'-style ecosystem indexes. (Distinct from project-discovery-feed, which re-publishes on a schedule, and free-resource-portal, which fronts a live service.)

name: OSS Project Discovery Feed
definition: A periodically refreshed feed, ranking, or chart that surfaces newly-interesting OSS projects on a recurring cadence — the repo is regenerated over time. e.g. HelloGitHub monthly issues, GitHub-Chinese-Top-Charts, trending-repo digests. (Distinct from awesome-list, a static one-shot index, and tech-newsletter-digest, which curates articles/ideas rather than ranking repos.)

name: Config / Template Boilerplate
definition: A repo whose payload is reusable config/template files you copy into a project as-is — the files ARE the deliverable, no prose. e.g. .gitignore template collections, EditorConfig/Prettier/tsconfig starters, license-file templates. (Distinct from code-style-guide, which is advice to read rather than files to drop in.)

name: Code Style / Best-Practices Guide
definition: An opinionated written guide prescribing conventions, style, or best practices for a language/stack — prose rules a developer reads, not a linter or template. e.g. airbnb/javascript style guide, nodebestpractices, Google engineering practices. (Distinct from config-template-boilerplate, which ships droppable files instead of advice.)

name: Prompt / Tool-Internals Dataset
definition: A curated dataset of prompts or reverse-engineered AI tool internals, meant to be consumed as data by people or models. e.g. prompts.chat collections, leaked/extracted system-prompts of AI coding tools, jailbreak/prompt-engineering corpora. (Distinct from non-software-knowledge — this data is specifically about LLMs/AI tooling.)

name: Non-Software Knowledge Collection
definition: A curated collection of human knowledge that is NOT about building software — reference content consumed by people, not ingested by tools. e.g. cooking recipes, math/physics study notes, history or language references, general how-to manuals. (Distinct from security-wordlist-dataset and prompt-dataset, whose data is machine input for tools.)

name: Algorithm / Reference-Impl Collection
definition: A collection of worked algorithm or data-structure implementations / solution walkthroughs whose purpose is to study HOW classic problems are solved, organized as reference code to learn from. e.g. multi-language algorithm libraries (TheAlgorithms), illustrated DS&A learning repos (hello-algo), LeetCode/interview solution guides (fucking-algorithm).

name: Career Roadmap / Study Guide
definition: An opinionated roadmap or interview/CS study guide that maps a sequence of WHAT to learn (skills, topics, milestones) without teaching the material itself — it points the way rather than walking you through lessons or code. e.g. dev/role roadmaps, system-design or coding-interview prep guides, 'things every X should know' lists (developer-roadmap, system-design-primer, JavaGuide).

name: Interactive Curriculum / Coding School
definition: A full structured curriculum or coding-school platform — an end-to-end program with ordered tracks/modules a learner progresses through, more than a single course or topic. e.g. a complete self-taught CS degree path (ossu/computer-science), an interactive learn-to-code platform/curriculum (freeCodeCamp).

name: Programming Course / Tutorial
definition: A multi-lesson course or tutorial series that actively teaches one language, framework, or topic from scratch through sequenced explanations and exercises — but is just content (a repo of lessons), not a hosted school platform. e.g. a language course (Python-100-Days), a topic/AI skill course (generative-ai-for-beginners), a multi-part hands-on tutorial.

name: Book / Cheatsheet Collection
definition: Long-form reading material or aggregated reference text for learning: full books, cheatsheets, or curated paper/reading lists meant to be read rather than progressed through as a course. e.g. an online book (You-Dont-Know-JS), a free-books or cheatsheet aggregation (free-programming-books), a papers reading list (papers-we-love).

name: Project-Based / Build-It Tutorial
definition: A learn-by-rebuilding guide that teaches by having you recreate a real technology or project from scratch, step by step — the deliverable is the build process, not finished reference code. e.g. 'build your own X' clone-it tutorials (build-your-own-x), curated project-based learning indexes (project-based-learning), a from-scratch 'write your own database/git' walkthrough.

name: Game / App Engine
definition: A full engine + editor for authoring interactive 2D/3D games or simulations, with a scene graph, asset pipeline and game loop (not just a UI/app framework). e.g. Godot, Bevy, a custom rendering/game-loop engine with an editor.

name: Client Library / SDK
definition: A reusable library or SDK that wraps a specific external API, protocol, or service so developers call it from their own code, not a standalone app. e.g. an official cloud-provider SDK, a Stripe/Twilio API wrapper, a database driver or gRPC/GraphQL client library.

name: Database Engine / Data Store
definition: A standalone database or data-store server whose primary product IS the storage/query engine you connect a client to (not a BaaS, not an app framework). e.g. relational/NewSQL engines (Postgres-likes), document/KV/columnar stores, vector/search/time-series engines.

name: Blockchain / Crypto Node
definition: A full source implementation of a blockchain, cryptocurrency, or distributed-ledger node — the protocol/consensus client itself, not a generic database or backend. e.g. L1 node clients, EVM/chain execution clients, validator/consensus node implementations.

name: Data Integration / ELT Platform
definition: A self-hostable platform whose job is moving/replicating data between sources and destinations via connectors and ELT/CDC pipelines — focused on data transport, not app automation or compute scheduling. e.g. Airbyte/Meltano-style ELT, CDC/replication tools, connector-based ingestion platforms.

name: Distributed Transaction Middleware
definition: A framework/middleware that coordinates distributed transactions and consistency across services (saga/2PC/TCC) — a library you embed for cross-service atomicity, not a full platform or database. e.g. Seata-style transaction coordinators, saga/2PC orchestration libraries, distributed-commit middleware.

name: Full-Stack App Starter / Boilerplate
definition: An opinionated, runnable scaffold/boilerplate wiring a server plus client (and often auth/DB config) into a ready-to-clone starter app — the value is the pre-assembled project skeleton, not a reusable library. e.g. T3/Next+API starters, MERN/Django+React boilerplates, SaaS-starter kits.

name: Package & Version Manager
definition: A command-line tool that resolves, installs, locks, or switches between dependency packages and/or language-runtime versions. e.g. package installers/resolvers (npm, pip, cargo, composer), runtime version switchers (pyenv, nvm, asdf), monorepo dependency managers. NOT a tool that merely downloads media files, and NOT a patcher of installed software.

name: Protocol / Open Standard Spec
definition: An open protocol or standard specification document defining wire formats, message schemas, or interop rules — a spec to implement against, not a runnable library or app. e.g. an RFC-style protocol spec, an open API/format standard, a messaging or transport interop standard. (Distinct from config-template-boilerplate: a spec describes behavior, it is not a file you drop in.)

name: Security & Reverse-Engineering Tool
definition: An offensive/defensive security or reverse-engineering tool for analyzing, exploiting, scanning, or auditing systems and binaries. e.g. a vulnerability/port scanner, a disassembler or binary-analysis framework, a pentest/exploit toolkit or fuzzer.

name: Open-Source Hardware / Firmware Project
definition: An open-source hardware design or device firmware project — schematics, PCB/board files, or embedded firmware for physical devices. e.g. a keyboard/QMK firmware, an Arduino/ESP32 device firmware, an open-hardware board or 3D-printer firmware.

name: Debugger / Language Tooling
definition: Low-level language tooling for inspecting or processing code at runtime or compile time — debuggers, profilers, linters, formatters, parsers, and language servers. e.g. a step debugger or profiler, a linter/formatter, a parser/AST library or LSP language server.

name: Web Build Tool / Bundler
definition: A web/JS build tool, bundler, transpiler, or task runner that compiles and packages frontend assets for shipping. e.g. a module bundler, a JS/TS transpiler or minifier, an asset/build-pipeline task runner like a webpack/vite/esbuild-class tool.

name: DevOps / Infra Management Client
definition: A client app or CLI for operators to manage and administer infrastructure/DevOps platforms — provisioning, deploying, or controlling cloud, containers, or clusters interactively. e.g. a Kubernetes dashboard/TUI, a cloud-console or Terraform-management client, a container/orchestration admin GUI.

name: Desktop GUI Application
definition: An installable native desktop application whose primary form is a packaged GUI binary running locally on the user's machine (not a server you deploy, not a creative canvas). e.g. password manager, OCR/document utility, image/file utility, calculator.

name: Consumer Mobile App
definition: A standalone end-user app distributed as an Android/iOS mobile binary, installed on a phone rather than self-hosted or run on desktop. e.g. a native Android utility app, an iOS productivity/tracking app, a mobile client published to an app store.

name: Secure File Transfer Tool
definition: A tool whose core purpose is securely transferring files directly between machines via short codes, relay servers, or peer-to-peer protocols. File transfer itself, not desktop/device control or stream aggregation. e.g. code-based encrypted file send tools (magic-wormhole, croc), P2P file-drop utilities, LAN secure transfer apps.

name: Hardware / Platform Emulator
definition: Software that emulates a physical hardware platform or game console, translating its native binary/firmware to run on a different host machine. e.g. a game-console emulator (PS4, Switch, 3DS), a CPU/machine emulator (QEMU-style), a retro-system emulator. NOT a software language VM (language-runtime) or an OS kernel (os-kernel).

name: Server-Side Web Framework
definition: An importable server-side library/framework for building HTTP/web apps and APIs in your own codebase — you depend on it as a package, it is not a runnable platform or scaffold. e.g. web frameworks (Express/Fastify/Flask/Gin), API/RPC frameworks, routing+middleware toolkits.

name: Test / Browser Automation Framework
definition: A framework or driver for automating browsers or end-to-end/UI tests by programmatically driving a real or headless browser. e.g. a Playwright/Selenium/Puppeteer-style automation driver, an E2E test runner that controls a browser, a web-scraping automation framework.

name: Computer Vision / Image Processing Library
definition: A foundational library of classical image/video processing PRIMITIVES — filtering, transforms, feature detection, geometry — not a trainable neural-network framework and not a single packaged model. Route here for general-purpose CV building blocks. e.g. image-processing toolkits (opencv, pillow/scikit-image), feature-detection/geometry libs, video-frame manipulation utilities.

name: Monitoring / Observability Platform
definition: A self-hostable observability platform purpose-built to watch other systems — collecting metrics/logs/traces or checking uptime, with alerting, dashboards, or status pages (route here only when monitoring IS the product, not a generic app that happens to log). e.g. uptime/status-page monitor (uptime-kuma), metrics/dashboard stack (netdata, grafana).

name: UI Component Development Workshop
definition: A workbench for building, previewing, and testing UI components in isolation, separate from a running app. e.g. a Storybook-style component explorer, a design-system/component playground, a visual component-test/snapshot harness.

name: Animation Engine / Library
definition: Library whose primary job is motion — interpolating/tweening values over time or programmatically composing animated scenes — distinct from static viz, scene rendering, or component kits. e.g. animation/tween engines (GSAP, Motion/Framer Motion, anime.js), programmatic scene-animation frameworks (Manim, Motion Canvas).

name: Recommender System Codebase
definition: A codebase for large-scale recommendation, personalization, or feed/search RANKING — candidate generation, retrieval, and ranking models built for serving recommendations specifically. Route here only when recommendation/ranking is the core purpose, not generic ML. e.g. recommender frameworks/toolkits, retrieval-and-ranking pipelines, collaborative-filtering/feed-ranking systems.

name: TUI / Terminal UI App
definition: An interactive full-screen terminal UI application built on a TUI framework to drive tools or workflows from the keyboard. e.g. cluster/process dashboards (k9s, lazygit), terminal file/DB browsers, TUI task managers. Defined by its interactive rendered interface, NOT by what it downloads, scrapes, or patches.

name: Programming Font / Typography Asset
definition: A monospaced programming font or typography asset designed for code, including glyph/ligature sets and font-tooling. e.g. a coding font with ligatures, a Nerd Font / icon-patched font, a font-patcher or glyph-asset pack.

name: Mock API / Fake Server Tool
definition: A tool that stands up a fake/mock backend or stub server to simulate API responses for development and testing, rather than calling a real service. e.g. a mock REST/GraphQL server, an HTTP request stubbing/interception library, a fixture-driven fake-API generator.

name: API Client / Testing Tool
definition: An interactive client app for manually exploring, sending, and testing requests against real APIs (not for wrapping one in code, and not a fake server). e.g. a Postman/Insomnia-style REST client, a GraphQL/gRPC request explorer, an HTTP request-testing GUI or TUI.

name: CI/CD Workflow Runner
definition: A continuous-integration/continuous-delivery engine or self-hosted workflow runner that executes pipelines on commits/events. e.g. a CI server or build agent, a self-hosted GitHub-Actions-style runner, a pipeline/workflow orchestration engine for builds and deploys.

name: Security Wordlist / Payload Dataset
definition: A curated collection of wordlists, fuzzing payloads, or attack data used as INPUT by offensive-security tools and pentesters. e.g. SecLists, PayloadsAllTheThings, password/subdomain/fuzz dictionaries. (Distinct from non-software-knowledge, which is human reading material, and prompt-dataset, which targets LLMs not exploitation.)

name: Labor Rights / Social Movement Repo
definition: A repo whose payload is a social, labor, or political CAUSE — manifestos, blacklists/whitelists of bad actors, protest licenses, or organizing resources — where the advocacy IS the artifact, not running software or a reading list. e.g. a worker-rights protest repo (996.ICU-style), an anti-corporate blacklist/manifesto, a movement license draft or civic-action toolkit. (Distinct from awesome-list/book-cheatsheet, which catalog resources, and code-style-guide, which prescribes engineering conventions.)

name: Free Resource / Service Portal
definition: A repo that fronts the site/docs of a live FREE public service, pointing users to claimable real-world resources behind it. e.g. free-domain/subdomain registries, free hosting or TLS-cert offer portals, free developer-credit listings. (Distinct from awesome-list: here a real service is offered, not just links cataloged.)

name: LLM App Template Cookbook
definition: A curated COLLECTION of ready-to-run, self-contained LLM/AI-agent starter templates meant to be cloned and customized — many small examples, not one library (llm-app-framework) or one runnable product (agent-platform). e.g. a repo of RAG/agent/voice starter apps, an awesome-style template gallery, a multi-stack AI cookbook of runnable demos.

name: Periodic Tech Newsletter / Digest
definition: A periodically-published tech newsletter or digest with editorial commentary curating articles, tools, and ideas for readers — issues accumulate over time. e.g. ruanyf/weekly, a weekly dev-news roundup, a themed editorial digest. (Distinct from project-discovery-feed, which ranks OSS repos, and awesome-list, a static link index.)

name: Protocol Reference Server Collection
definition: A curated collection of REFERENCE server/client implementations that demonstrate how to build for an AI protocol or open standard (e.g. MCP) — example servers, not a generic agent-platform or an importable SDK. e.g. an official MCP reference-servers monorepo, a set of protocol example connectors/clients, a spec's sample-implementation bundle.

name: Browser Extension / Add-on
definition: A browser-installed extension or add-on (content blocker, page enhancer, productivity injector) that runs inside Chrome/Firefox/Safari, NOT a standalone app (desktop-gui-app) or a coding-agent plugin (agent-extension-pack). e.g. an ad/content blocker (uBlock-style), a markdown/page-rendering add-on, a tab/productivity extension.

name: Static Site / Docs Generator
definition: A framework or tool whose job is to turn Markdown/source into a static documentation or content website, distinct from a general web-ui-framework (builds apps) or web-build-bundler (bundles assets). e.g. a docs-site framework (Docusaurus-style), an API-docs generator (Slate-style), a static-site generator.

name: Stream Processing / Distributed Compute Engine
definition: An engine for large-scale batch or streaming data computation across a cluster, distinct from data-integration-platform (ELT/connectors), database-engine (storage), or message-queue (transport). e.g. a distributed compute engine (Spark/Ray-style), a real-time stream/dataflow processor (Pathway-style).

name: Version Control System
definition: The core version-control engine itself that tracks source history (commit graph, branching, diffs), NOT a hosting platform, GUI client, or CI runner. e.g. a distributed VCS (Git/Mercurial-style), a next-gen source-control engine.

name: Robotics / Autonomous Vehicle Stack
definition: A full software stack for controlling physical robots or autonomous vehicles (perception, planning, control), distinct from a generic ml-framework or simulation library. e.g. a self-driving/ADAS stack (openpilot-style), a robotics middleware/autonomy framework.

name: Media Processing / Codec Library
definition: A library/toolkit for encoding, decoding, transcoding, or transforming audio/video/image streams, distinct from a media-downloader (fetches), media player (plays), or creative-visual-app (edits via GUI). e.g. a multimedia codec/transcode framework (FFmpeg/GStreamer-style), an image-processing codec library.

name: Numeric / DataFrame Library
definition: A foundational library for in-memory numeric arrays, tensors, or tabular DataFrames used as the substrate for analysis and ML, distinct from an ml-framework (models/training) or data-viz-library (plots). e.g. an N-dimensional array library (NumPy-style), a DataFrame library (pandas/Polars-style).

name: Presentation / Slides Framework
definition: A framework for authoring slide decks or presentations as code (Markdown/HTML/JS), distinct from a docs-site-generator (doc websites) or a general web-ui-framework. e.g. a code-driven slides framework (Slidev/reveal.js-style), an HTML presentation engine (impress.js-style).

name: Infrastructure-as-Code / Provisioning Tool
definition: A tool that declaratively provisions and manages cloud/infra resources from code, distinct from infra-orchestration (runs/schedules workloads) or devops-management-client (GUI admin). e.g. a declarative provisioning tool (Terraform/Pulumi-style), a serverless deploy framework (Serverless-style).

name: Proxy / Circumvention Core Engine
definition: The headless core/daemon implementing a proxy or censorship-circumvention protocol (VMess/VLESS/Trojan/Shadowsocks), distinct from a proxy-client (GUI), reverse-proxy-tunnel (ingress), or free-resource feed. e.g. a proxy protocol core (V2Ray/Xray/sing-box-style), a circumvention engine (XX-Net-style).

name: Test Framework / Runner
definition: A framework or runner for writing and executing unit/integration tests with assertions, mocking, and reporting, distinct from browser-automation-framework (e2e/browser drivers) or api-client-tool. e.g. a JS test runner (Jest/Vitest-style), an xUnit-style testing framework.

name: Quantitative Trading Platform
definition: A platform/framework for quantitative finance: backtesting, strategy research, live algorithmic trading, distinct from a generic ml-framework or numeric-dataframe-library. e.g. a quant research/backtest platform (Qlib-style), an event-driven algo-trading framework (vnpy-style).

name: API / LLM Gateway
definition: A gateway/proxy that fronts upstream APIs or LLM providers with routing, auth, rate-limiting, and a unified interface, distinct from reverse-proxy-tunnel (raw L4/L7 ingress) or an llm-app-framework. e.g. a general API gateway (Kong-style), a unified multi-provider LLM router (LiteLLM-style).

name: Process Manager / Supervisor
definition: A daemon/CLI that launches, monitors, restarts, and load-balances long-running processes, distinct from infra-orchestration (cluster schedulers) or a single-app server. e.g. a Node process manager (PM2-style), a process supervisor/init (supervisord-style).

name: TUI Framework / Library
definition: A library/framework for BUILDING rich terminal user interfaces (layout, widgets, event loop), distinct from tui-app (a finished TUI application you run) or terminal-console (the emulator). e.g. a Go TUI framework (Bubble Tea-style), a Python TUI toolkit (Textual-style).

name: Message Queue / Event Streaming Platform
definition: A broker for asynchronous messaging or durable event streaming between services, distinct from stream-processing-engine (computes over data) or database-engine (storage). e.g. a distributed log/streaming platform (Kafka/Pulsar-style), a message broker (RabbitMQ-style).

name: Vector Search / ANN Library
definition: A library or engine for approximate-nearest-neighbor and similarity search over high-dimensional embeddings, distinct from a full database-engine or recommender-system. e.g. an ANN similarity-search library (FAISS-style), a vector index/embeddings search engine.

name: Embedded Storage / Database Library
definition: An in-process storage engine or database-access library linked into an application (key-value store, ORM), distinct from a standalone database-engine (its own server) or backend-data-platform. e.g. an embedded key-value store (LevelDB/RocksDB-style), an ORM/data-access library (GORM-style).

name: Low-Code / Internal-Tool Builder
definition: A self-hosted platform or framework for visually building internal tools, admin panels, dashboards, or schemas with minimal code, distinct from a frontend-scaffolder (generates a codebase) or a hand-coded ui-component-kit. e.g. a low-code internal-tool builder (ToolJet/Retool-style), an admin/CRUD framework (Refine-style), a visual DB-schema designer (drawDB-style).

name: Monorepo / Build Orchestration Tool
definition: A tool that manages multi-package monorepos: task orchestration, dependency graphs, caching, versioning/publishing, distinct from a web-build-bundler (bundles one app) or package-version-manager (installs deps). e.g. a JS monorepo orchestrator (Lerna/Nx/Turborepo-style).

name: Architecture / Best-Practice Reference App
definition: A reference codebase demonstrating recommended app architecture and best practices for a stack/framework, meant to be studied or copied, distinct from a project-based-tutorial (step-by-step build) or algorithm-reference-impl (algorithms). e.g. an official architecture-samples repo, a production-structure reference (bulletproof-react-style), a framework-feature demo collection (spring-boot-demo-style).

name: Generalist Mega-Pack / Marketplace
definition: Broad multi-category bundles or marketplaces mixing skills, agents, hooks, and commands with no single domain focus.

name: Dev-Workflow & Methodology Pack
definition: Packs encoding engineering discipline — TDD, spec-driven, agile, YAGNI, meta-prompting — to shape how agents build.

name: Persona & Orchestration Pack
definition: Agent persona libraries plus multi-agent team/orchestration CLIs that coordinate workers across harnesses.

name: Code-Graph & Memory Context Pack
definition: Tooling that gives agents durable context — code knowledge graphs, persistent memory, and output/context compression.

name: Design & UI Taste Pack
definition: Frontend/UI design rule packs that steer agents away from AI slop toward better layout, motion, and typography.

name: Domain-Specialist Skill Pack
definition: Skill packs for a non-coding vertical — careers, marketing, research, note-taking, academia.

name: Media Player & Editor
definition: Desktop apps for playing, recording, editing or processing video/audio/images (players, screen capture, OCR, upscaling).

name: Music Player & Downloader
definition: Desktop clients focused on streaming-music playback and download management.

name: Web Browser & Engine
definition: Standalone desktop web browsers and from-scratch browser/rendering engines.

name: Note, Editor & Knowledge
definition: Desktop markdown/WYSIWYG editors, note-taking and personal-knowledge apps.

name: System Monitor & Control
definition: Menu-bar/tray utilities monitoring or controlling system resources, network, displays and small desktop helpers.

name: Developer & Data Tool
definition: Desktop GUIs for databases, data inspection, model visualization and developer/data workflows.

name: Security, Privacy & Messaging
definition: Desktop apps for credentials, encryption, chat/message extraction and private messaging clients.

name: File & Disk Utility
definition: Desktop file managers, torrent clients and disk/USB flashing utilities.

name: Language & Framework Ecosystem
definition: Awesome lists indexing a single programming language or app framework ecosystem (Python, Go, Rust, React, iOS, Flutter, etc.).

name: AI, Agents & LLM Tooling
definition: Curated indexes of LLM apps, AI agents, Claude/Cursor/OpenClaw skills, AI-coding rules, and ready-to-run AI/automation workflows.

name: Self-Hosted Apps & Sysadmin Tools
definition: Indexes of self-hostable services, open-source desktop apps, sysadmin/devops tooling, Docker, and shell utilities.

name: Careers, Jobs & Interviews
definition: Curated indexes for tech careers: internships, remote jobs, no-whiteboard hiring, interview-question banks, and CTO reading.

name: CS Learning & Education
definition: Indexes of CS courses, books, design patterns, system-design and architecture resources, and essential developer reading.

name: Design & Creative Resources
definition: Curated indexes of design tools, free design assets (fonts/icons/UI kits), and design-doc/markdown resources.

name: Meta-Index, Data & Misc Resources
definition: Catch-all: meta-awesome-lists, public-API/dataset catalogs, free-tier/free-resource directories, and content/reading hubs.

name: Infrastructure & DevOps
definition: Self-hosted servers, PaaS/deployment, container & VPS management, observability, backup, git hosting and developer-platform tooling.

name: Media & Photos
definition: Self-hosted media servers, photo libraries, game streaming, NVR/camera and media-downloader apps.

name: Knowledge, Notes & Docs
definition: Self-hosted note-taking, knowledge bases, wikis, CMS/blogging, e-readers and documentation sites.

name: Productivity & Business
definition: Self-hosted project management, CRM, ERP, scheduling, resume builders and no-code DB/app platforms.

name: Communication & Social
definition: Self-hosted chat, team comms, federated social, community forums and customer-support platforms.

name: Files, Sync & Storage
definition: Self-hosted file managers, sync engines, cloud storage, document management and file-sharing servers.

name: Network, Privacy & Security
definition: Self-hosted DNS/ad-blockers, VPN/proxy panels, password managers and content-filtering tools.

name: AI, Data & Finance
definition: Self-hosted LLM/RAG/AI engines, BI & analytics, personal finance/trading, and data/web utility tools.

name: HTTP / Networking Client
definition: HTTP, RPC, real-time, and web-framework client/server transport libraries for talking over the network.

name: Frontend State / Async
definition: Client-side state management, server-state/data-fetching, reactive streams, and immutable data libraries.

name: Database / ORM Client
definition: ORMs, query builders, and database connection/client libraries.

name: UI Rendering / Widget
definition: UI component, graphics, animation, media-player, and DOM/widget rendering libraries.

name: Text / Document Parsing
definition: Rich-text editors and parsers/renderers for markup, documents, spreadsheets, OCR, and NLP text.

name: Data / ML / Scraping
definition: DataFrames, vector/ML, RL, scraping, multimedia, trading, and LLM-gateway data-processing libraries.

name: Forms / Schema Validation
definition: Form state libraries and schema definition/validation/serialization libraries.

name: General Utility / Helpers
definition: General-purpose utility, date/time, terminal, and grab-bag helper libraries.

name: Dev Tooling / Framework
definition: Developer tooling and frameworks: browser automation, CLI/TUI, testing, build/git hooks, type defs, and contract/header libraries.

name: Editor / App Plugin
definition: A plugin, extension, mod, or injector that adds features to an existing host editor or desktop app rather than standing alone; e.g. VSCodeVim, lualine.nvim, obsidian-dataview, BetterDiscord, ComfyUI-Manager, decky-loader, raycast/extensions.

name: Android Modding / Hooking Framework
definition: Xposed/Magisk/Zygisk-style frameworks and modules that hook or patch Android apps and system runtime; e.g. LSPosed, ZygiskNext, BiliRoaming, AndResGuard.

name: Job / Task Scheduler
definition: Library or framework for scheduling, queuing, and running background/cron/distributed jobs; e.g. celery, xxl-job, apscheduler, quartznet, gocron.

name: Load / Performance Testing Tool
definition: Tool for load, stress, and performance testing of services under simulated traffic; e.g. k6, locust.

name: Game Dev Library / Middleware
definition: Building-block library or middleware for building games (ECS, physics, netcode, engine plugin) rather than a full engine; e.g. entt, box2d, bullet3, Mirror, BepInEx, FastLED.

name: Physics / Robotics Simulator
definition: Physics or embodied-AI simulator used for robotics, control, and RL training; e.g. mujoco, genesis-world, pybullet.

name: Native Build System / Compiler Cache
definition: Native/C/C++ build system, build generator, or compiler-cache wrapper; e.g. meson, xmake, sccache, Bear.

name: Memory Allocator
definition: Drop-in malloc/system memory allocator library; e.g. mimalloc, jemalloc.

name: Icon / SVG Asset Pack
definition: Set of reusable icons or SVG assets shipped as a library/pack; e.g. feather, simple-icons, tabler-icons, ionicons.

name: Theme / Color-Scheme Pack
definition: Color scheme, desktop theme, icon theme, or site template distributed as a styling asset; e.g. dracula-theme, nord, arc-theme, papirus-icon-theme, hexo themes.

name: RL Environment / Testbed
definition: Reinforcement-learning environment, game wrapper, or agent testbed; e.g. pysc2, deepmind/lab.

name: Model Merging / Weight-Editing Tool
definition: Tool that merges, edits, or surgically manipulates trained model weights; e.g. mergekit, heretic.

name: Agent Sandbox / Code-Execution Runtime
definition: Sandboxed, hardened runtime for executing agent-generated code safely; e.g. E2B, OpenSandbox, NemoClaw.

name: Agent Memory / Context Store
definition: Persistence layer or server for long-term agent memory and context; e.g. agentmemory, memvid, OpenViking.

name: Templating / View Engine
definition: Server-side text/HTML templating or view engine library; e.g. jinja, liquid, ejs.

name: Distributed / Network Storage Platform
definition: Distributed, object, or network filesystem and storage platform; e.g. ceph, zfs, deepseek 3FS, s3fs-fuse.

name: Firmware Flash / Bootloader Tool
definition: Tool that flashes firmware or acts as a bootloader/firmware loader for hardware; e.g. esptool, OpenCorePkg.

name: Resilience / Flow-Control Middleware
definition: Fault-tolerance, circuit-breaker, rate-limit, or flow-control middleware; e.g. Hystrix, Sentinel.

name: Dataset Collection
definition: Raw dataset shipped as a repo: time-series, training, or labeled data; e.g. COVID-19, quickdraw-dataset.

name: OS Image / Distribution
definition: Prebuilt OS image, Linux distribution, or container base image (not the kernel itself); e.g. openwrt, DietPi, nixpkgs, distroless, runner-images.

name: Display Server / Compositor / Window Manager
definition: Display servers, Wayland/X11 compositors and tiling window managers — the graphical session layer. e.g. swaywm/wlroots, Airblader/i3, riverwm/river, WayfireWM/wayfire, leftwm/leftwm.

name: Game Clone / Decompilation / Source Port
definition: Open-source reimplementations, decompilations and source ports of existing games or ROMs. e.g. OpenXcom/OpenXcom, id-Software/wolf3d, zeldaret/mm, HarbourMasters/SpaghettiKart, hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp.

name: Game Mod / Plugin / Injector
definition: Mods, plugins, trainers, graphics injectors and memory-hacking frameworks that modify existing games. e.g. MeteorDevelopment/meteor-client, DFHack/dfhack, emoose/DLSSTweaks, EssentialsX/Essentials, NVIDIAGameWorks/rtx-remix.

name: Scientific / Numerical Computing Library
definition: Domain scientific and numerical computing libraries — physics, chemistry, astronomy, FEM, ODE/PDE, signal/imaging. e.g. astropy/astropy, root-project/root, pyscf/pyscf, SciML/DifferentialEquations.jl, mfem/mfem.

name: Mathematical Optimization / Solver Library
definition: Mathematical optimization modeling languages and numerical solvers (LP/MIP/NLP/convex/blackbox). e.g. coin-or/pulp, jump-dev/JuMP.jl, ERGO-Code/HiGHS, Pyomo/pyomo, coin-or/Ipopt.

name: ML / LLM Eval & Benchmark Harness
definition: Frameworks, harnesses and suites for evaluating and benchmarking ML/LLM models. e.g. embeddings-benchmark/mteb, google/BIG-bench, huggingface/lighteval, beir-cellar/beir, Vchitect/VBench.

name: ML Explainability / Interpretability Library
definition: Libraries for model explainability, interpretability, debugging and responsible-AI evaluation. e.g. TeamHG-Memex/eli5, SeldonIO/alibi, oegedijk/explainerdashboard, microsoft/responsible-ai-toolbox.

name: Mobile App Modding / Tweak / Hook
definition: iOS/Android app patching, hooking, tweaks and sideload mods for existing mobile apps. e.g. Naituw/IPAPatch, QiuChenly/CoreInject, MiRO92/uYou-for-YouTube, whoeevee/EeveeSpotifyReborn, buginux/WeChatRedEnvelop.

name: Concurrency / Async Runtime Library
definition: Low-level concurrency primitives, coroutine/fiber and async event-loop runtime libraries. e.g. mitchellh/libxev, enki/libev, hnes/libaco, Amanieu/parking_lot, agronholm/anyio.

name: FFI / Binding Generator
definition: Tools that generate cross-language bindings, FFI glue or stubs from headers/IDLs. e.g. mozilla/cbindgen, mono/CppSharp, fzyzcjy/flutter_rust_bridge, PyO3/maturin, kaitai-io/kaitai_struct.

name: Schema / API Code Generator
definition: Code generators driven by schemas, IDLs or API specs (OpenAPI/IDL/SQL → code/docs). e.g. smithy-lang/smithy, tfranzel/drf-spectacular, kubb-labs/kubb, microsoft/bond, rswag/rswag.

name: GPU / Parallel Compute Library
definition: GPU and heterogeneous parallel-compute libraries, primitives and portability SDKs. e.g. ROCm/hip, NVIDIA/cccl, KomputeProject/kompute, moderngpu/moderngpu, rapidsai/cugraph.

name: EDA / Chip-Design Toolchain
definition: Electronic design automation, FPGA/ASIC synthesis and chip-design flows. e.g. YosysHQ/yosys, YosysHQ/nextpnr, The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenLane, The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD.

name: Static-Site Theme / Template Pack
definition: Themes, skins and templates for static-site generators (Hexo/Hugo/Jekyll/Gatsby) and portfolio sites. e.g. jekyll/minima, next-theme/hexo-theme-next, olOwOlo/hugo-theme-even, LekoArts/gatsby-themes, rammcodes/Dopefolio.

name: Proxy / VPN Subscription Feed
definition: Curated proxy/VPN node subscription feeds, rotators, config lists and rule datasets. e.g. awesome-vpn/awesome-vpn, bestruirui/BestSub, barry-far/V2ray-Config, henson/proxypool, runetfreedom/russia-v2ray-rules-dat.

name: Font / Typography Asset Pack
definition: Distributable font families and typography asset packs (non-programming-specific). e.g. rastikerdar/vazirmatn, welai/glow-sans, Chenyu-otf/chenyuluoyan_thin.

name: Formal Verification / Theorem-Proving Tool
definition: Program verifiers, proof assistants and theorem-prover libraries. e.g. verus-lang/verus, creusot-rs/creusot, leanprover-community/mathlib4.

name: Cryptography / ZK / FHE Library
definition: Cryptographic primitive libraries — PKI, zero-knowledge proofs, fully-homomorphic encryption. e.g. tjfoc/gmsm, kjur/jsrsasign, scipr-lab/libsnark, zama-ai/tfhe-rs, google/fully-homomorphic-encryption.

name: Internationalization / Localization Library
definition: Internationalization, localization and locale-data frameworks and libraries. e.g. opral/inlang, unicode-org/icu4x, globalize/globalize.

name: Native Mobile UI Component / Widget
definition: Single-purpose native iOS/Android UI components, widgets and presentation libraries. e.g. cruffenach/CRToast, slackhq/PanModal, jd-alexander/LikeButton, Ramotion/reel-search, dmytrodanylyk/shadow-layout.

name: Geometry / Spatial / GIS Library
definition: Computational-geometry, spatial-indexing and GIS libraries. e.g. google/s2geometry, locationtech/jts, NetTopologySuite/NetTopologySuite, mourner/suncalc.

name: Vendor Issue-Tracker / Roadmap Mirror
definition: Repos that exist mainly as a public issue tracker, roadmap or release/changelog mirror for a (often closed-source) product. e.g. ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux, aws/containers-roadmap, docker/for-mac, microsoft/vscode-remote-release.

name: Embedded Systems / MCU Library
definition: Reusable C/C++ libraries targeting microcontrollers/embedded systems: libc/runtime support, ring buffers, drivers, embedded display/GUI rendering. e.g. picolibc, lwrb, u8glib, UGUI.

name: C / C++ Systems Library
definition: Foundational C/C++ systems-language building blocks: ADT/macro/type utilities, stdlib polyfills/backports, concurrent/lock-free data structures, sparse-matrix & numerical primitives. e.g. datatype99, gulrak/filesystem, junction, SuiteSparse.

name: Language Binding / Interop Library
definition: Reusable libraries that bridge two languages or runtimes (Rust<->C++/Qt, JS<->native, JVM/.NET<->accelerator), enabling cross-language FFI, codegen, or accelerator dispatch. e.g. cxx-qt, TornadoVM.

name: Runnable Demo / Example Cookbook
definition: Curated collections of runnable demo scripts, starters, and mini-examples for a specific platform/stack, meant as browseable references rather than a single library. e.g. confluent demo-scene, javascript-mini-projects, GPU compute-shader examples.

name: Console Homebrew / Custom Firmware App
definition: Homebrew launchers, custom-firmware shells, and end-user mod tools that run on game consoles (Switch/3DS/DS/Wii) under CFW. e.g. nx-hbmenu, EdiZon, nds-bootstrap.

name: Prebuilt Binary / Repackaging Repo
definition: Repos whose value is fetching/repackaging upstream prebuilt binaries or wheels into a redistributable archive via CI, not source. e.g. flash-attention prebuilt wheels, poppler-windows.

name: Scientific / Domain-Analysis Library
definition: Importable domain-specific analytical libraries and runnable scientific pipelines (spatial stats, bioinformatics, genomics, econometrics) consumed by researchers. e.g. PySAL, vg, nf-core/rnaseq, pyquil.

name: Native Bridge Plugin (Cordova/Capacitor/Flutter)
definition: Reusable cross-platform-app plugins that bridge web/Flutter apps to native mobile SDKs (IAP, push, splash, native assets) via the framework's plugin interface. e.g. cordova-plugin-purchase, flutter_native_splash.

name: Router / OpenWrt Firmware Plugin
definition: Packages, plugins, or plugin hubs that extend router firmware (OpenWrt/LuCI, DD-WRT, Koolshare) with web-UI pages, hooks, or notification integrations installed on the router. e.g. luci-app-wechatpush, koolshare softcenter.

name: Security / Vulnerability Awareness Demo
definition: Minimal PoC pages or scripts demonstrating a security/privacy risk or historical vulnerability for education/archival, with no production capability. e.g. browser-autofill-phishing, novelty CVE demos.

name: Creative / Interactive Art Piece
definition: Small self-contained finished interactive/illustrative works (web or desktop toys, explorables, webcam toys) that exist as an art/education experience, not a reusable framework. e.g. ncase/wbwwb, ascii-camera.

name: Data Serialization / Parser Library
definition: Reusable libraries that parse/serialize/stream structured data formats (JSON/XML/YAML, regex/pattern engines) as importable dependencies. e.g. litjson, json-machine, pcre2.

name: Personal Social-Account Data Script
definition: Single-purpose scripts a user runs against their own social account (WeChat/Zhihu/QQ) via a reverse-engineered protocol to scrape, analyze, or bulk-clean their personal data. e.g. wechat_friends, dog-fucked-zhihu.

name: Static Reference / Docs Content Repo
definition: Repos whose payload is read-only written content: policy/standards docs, vendor docs source, localized doc translations, changelog/release-note indexes, version-template diffs. e.g. project-open-data, sp-dev-docs, node-api-cn, rn-diff-purge.

name: Personal Profile / Community Collection Repo
definition: Repos whose only artifact is a personal profile README or a community-submitted profile collection (graduating classes, event yearbooks), with no reusable software. e.g. vaquarkhan, GitHubGraduation-2022.

name: Windows API / Driver Compatibility Shim
definition: Drop-in DLL/driver shims that fix or remap legacy Windows graphics/API/device access for modern systems or retro compatibility. e.g. DDrawCompat, HidHide, hidusbf.

name: App-Specific Automation / Cheat Script
definition: Scripts/hooks that automate or cheat one specific commercial mobile app or game via ADB/Frida/accessibility, narrowly targeted rather than general automation. e.g. XiaoYuanKouSuan, autojs check-in scripts.

name: Build / Asset Pipeline Tool
definition: Domain-specific build, packaging, hot-update, or asset-pipeline tooling (game engine plugins, installers, portable packagers, build-time native asset generators). e.g. HotPatcher, ComfyUI-Easy-Install.

name: NLP / Text-Processing Library
definition: Natural-language text processing/analysis libs (tokenize, morphology, lang-detect, NLG, clustering). e.g. pymorphy2, lingua-rs, cltk, simplenlg, carrot2

name: SLAM / Visual Odometry Library
definition: Visual/visual-inertial SLAM and odometry reference impls & frameworks. e.g. dm-vio, GSLAM, DynaSLAM, R-VIO, badslam

name: ML Paper Reference Implementation
definition: Reference code reproducing a specific ML/CV/DL research paper. e.g. mixmatch, Word-As-Image, five-video-classification-methods

name: ML Data Prep / Labeling Library
definition: Datasets prep, cleaning, weak-supervision labeling & exploration libs for ML pipelines. e.g. lhotse, datacleaner, skweak, meerkat, iterative-stratification

name: Graph Analytics Library
definition: Graph statistics / community-detection / network-analysis libs. e.g. graspologic, leidenalg

name: Confidential Computing / TEE SDK
definition: Trusted-execution-environment / enclave SDKs & middleware. e.g. openenclave, YeeZ-Privacy-Computing

name: Feature Flag / Experimentation Platform
definition: Feature-toggle & experimentation libs/platforms. e.g. fun_with_flags, togglz, featurevisor

name: DI / IoC Container Library
definition: Dependency-injection / inversion-of-control container libs. e.g. Dip, nette/di

name: State Machine Library
definition: Finite-state-machine / state-management libs. e.g. statig, FlowRedux

name: Smart Contract / On-Chain Library
definition: Reusable smart-contract frameworks & on-chain primitive libs. e.g. thirdweb contracts, tapio-eth, permit2

name: IoT / Smart-Home Protocol Stack
definition: IoT/industrial/smart-home protocol stacks & gateways. e.g. esp-matter, eclipse smarthome, OpENer, jt808-server

name: Chat Bot Framework / SDK
definition: Frameworks/SDKs for building chat & messaging bots. e.g. sopel-irc, sapphiredev framework

name: Web Server Module / Plugin
definition: Nginx/web-server extension modules & plugins. e.g. ngx_http_geoip2, ngx_cache_purge, nginx-gridfs

name: Typesetting / Document Engine
definition: Typesetting systems & document-layout engines. e.g. SATySFi, MiKTeX

name: Source-to-Source Transpiler
definition: Cross-language / source-to-source transpilers. e.g. shift-js, metapensiero.pj

name: AOP / Code-Weaving Framework
definition: Aspect-oriented programming / code-weaving frameworks. e.g. aspectd, aspect-injector

name: Data Structure Library
definition: General-purpose data-structure / collection libs (graphs, vectors, tries). e.g. go-immutable-radix, alga, js-sdsl, c-vector

name: Serialization / Data-Format Library
definition: Object/data serialization & binary-format libs. e.g. nippy, twitter/Serial, ason

name: Compression / Codec Primitive Library
definition: Compression algorithm/codec primitive libs. e.g. smaz, density, TurboPFor

name: String Matching / Search Library
definition: Multi-pattern string-matching / Aho-Corasick libs. e.g. pyahocorasick, AhoCorasickDoubleArrayTrie

name: Notebook Kernel / REPL
definition: Jupyter/notebook language kernels & REPL backends. e.g. gonb, xeus

name: HDL / Digital-Design Library
definition: HDL component libs, verification frameworks & digital-circuit simulators. e.g. verilog-axis, VUnit, digitaljs

name: Audio Plugin Framework / Bridge
definition: Audio-plugin development frameworks, suites & host bridges. e.g. DPF, SPARTA, LinVst

name: Hypervisor / VMM
definition: Hypervisors & virtual-machine monitors. e.g. xen, MiniVisorPkg

name: Filesystem / Kernel Driver
definition: Filesystem & network kernel drivers / modules. e.g. linux-apfs, Ext3Fsd, tap-windows6

name: Home-Automation Integration
definition: Home-Assistant / smart-device integration plugins. e.g. kia_uvo, meross-homeassistant, tapo-p100, tesla

name: Game Source / Indie Game Project
definition: Source of original (non-clone) indie games. e.g. hawkthorne, keeperrl, RedRunner, swarm-game

name: Web Browser Polyfill / Shim
definition: Browser/web-platform polyfills & ponyfills. e.g. webcomponents/polyfills, respimage, standardized-audio-context

name: 3D-Printable / Parametric Model Pack
definition: 3D-printable hardware mods & parametric CAD model libs. e.g. voron, gridfinity_extended, loklak_3d, the-growroom

name: Creative Asset Pack
definition: Reusable game/design/sound/branding asset packs. e.g. superpowers-asset-packs, octave sounds, sketch-foundation-kit, bodyapps-artwork

name: Rule / Inference Engine Library
definition: Business-rules, decision, or inference engine libraries that evaluate rule sets against facts (e.g. deliveredtechnologies/rulebook, rencalo770/gengine, ulfurinn/wongi-engine).

name: Input Method Engine / Library
definition: Input method editors and pinyin/IME engines converting keystrokes to text (e.g. libpinyin, sunpinyin, fcitx5-rime).

name: EDA Footprint / Symbol Library
definition: Reusable PCB footprint, symbol, and 3D-model libraries for EDA tools like KiCad (e.g. KiCad/kicad-footprints, keebio/Keebio-Parts.pretty, ebastler/marbastlib).

name: Desktop Shell / Environment Extension
definition: GNOME/KDE/desktop-environment shell extensions and panel widgets (e.g. maniacx/Battery-Health-Charging, maoschanz/emoji-selector-for-gnome, LukeSmithxyz/dwmblocks).

name: Honeypot / Deception Platform
definition: Honeypots and deception-based defensive tools that lure/trap attackers (e.g. 0x4D31/galah, C4o/Juggler, utkusen/baitroute).

name: Captive Portal / Network Access Gateway
definition: Captive portals and network access controllers gating client connectivity (e.g. coova/coova-chilli, openNDS/openNDS).

name: SDR / Radio Signal Toolkit
definition: Software-defined-radio, RF and cellular/RAN signal-processing stacks, drivers and instruments; e.g. gnuradio/gr-osmosdr, RangeNetworks/OpenBTS-UMTS, NVIDIA/aerial-cuda-accelerated-ran, leswright1977/PySpectrometer2.

name: Industrial Automation / PLC Framework
definition: Industrial control, PLC/SCADA and fieldbus (Modbus/CAN) runtimes and frameworks for factory/machine automation; e.g. TcOpenGroup/TcOpen, qitechgmbh/control, steveohara/j2mod, Open-Agriculture/AgIsoStack-plus-plus.

name: Mining Pool Server
definition: Crypto mining-pool servers, stratum protocol implementations and miner proxies (server-side, distinct from a full chain node); e.g. stratum-mining/stratum, Crypto-Expert/stratum-mining, minerproxy-btc/RustMinerSystem.

name: ComfyUI / Generative Node Pack
definition: Custom node and workflow packs that extend ComfyUI / node-based generative-AI pipelines; e.g. LAOGOU-666/Comfyui_LG_Tools, shiimizu/ComfyUI_smZNodes, Aaalice233/ShiQi_Workflow.

name: Live-Coding Music Library
definition: Live-coding / algorave music DSLs and environments for performing and composing sound as code; e.g. Bubobubobubobubo/sardine, pjagielski/punkt, munshkr/flok, DimaSamoz/mezzo.

name: Packet-Processing / SDN Dataplane Engine
definition: Userspace high-speed packet-processing, software switches and programmable SDN dataplanes (often DPDK/kernel-bypass); e.g. NetSys/bess, lagopus/lagopus, tbarbette/fastclick, libmoon/libmoon.

name: Package Registry / Mirror Server
definition: Server-side package registries, artifact stores and mirror/cache proxies for package ecosystems; e.g. mamba-org/quetz, anatol/pacoloco.

name: CLI Framework / Builder Library
definition: Libraries and micro-frameworks for building command-line apps (arg parsing, commands, scaffolding); e.g. oclif/core, laravel-zero/framework, xcaeser/zli, Andarius/piou.

name: Network Routing / DNS Daemon
definition: Routing-protocol, RPKI and DNS infrastructure daemons and route/config automation (BGP, dynamic DNS, resolvers); e.g. bio-routing/bio-rd, cloudflare/gortr, NLnetLabs/krill, wolf-joe/ts-dns.
